questions.q: Where do Oracle's official SQL docs live?
options: dev.oracle.com/doc
docs.oracle.com
oracle.org/docs
learn.oracle.com
questions.explain: Oracle's official documentation is hosted at docs.oracle.com.

questions.q: In a typical syntax diagram, what do square brackets around a clause usually mean?
options: That clause is deprecated and should never be used
That clause only works in beta versions
That clause is optional
That clause is required and cannot be omitted
questions.explain: Square brackets are the standard convention for an optional element in a syntax diagram.

questions.q: As a developer (not a DBA) reading vendor docs, what should you focus on, and what can you usually skip?
options: Read every section on the page equally, since DBA and developer content can't be told apart
Focus on the syntax diagram and examples; skip surrounding sections on storage internals, memory configuration, and security permissions
Focus only on memory configuration settings since those matter most for query writing
Skip the syntax diagram entirely and only read the examples
questions.explain: The syntax diagram and examples are what a developer writing queries needs; admin-focused sections are out of scope for this course.

questions.q: Why do 'compatible with standard SQL' callouts in vendor docs matter so much for this course?
options: They only apply to administration features, not query syntax
They are purely historical trivia with no practical use
They tell you directly whether a feature will carry over to another platform, which is the exact skill this course builds
They indicate a feature is deprecated and will be removed soon
questions.explain: These callouts flag standard vs. vendor-specific behavior, directly answering the portability question this course is built around.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say to always check which version a doc page applies to?
options: Vendor docs never specify which version they describe, so this step is impossible
Dialect behavior can change meaningfully between major versions, like Oracle's IDENTITY columns which were only added in Oracle 12c
Version numbers are purely cosmetic and never affect SQL syntax
Only MySQL has version-specific documentation; the others never change
questions.explain: Oracle's IDENTITY column syntax, built on sequences, was only added in 12c -- a concrete example of version-specific behavior.
